newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's MEA increases capital by $47.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's MEA increases capital by $47.5 mln.

text.p: Lebanon's Middle East Airlines increased its capital on Saturday by $47.5 million to $178.75 million under a plan launched last July to rehabilitate the ailing airline.
The increase, a cash injection from shareholders approved at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting, is a part of a plan to raise the airline's capital by $225 million.

MEA Chairman Khaled Salam told reporters that the latest increase, the third tranche of the $225 million capital increase, will be used partially to meet remaining debts and for other needs by the airliner.
"Today the shareholders approved an increase of $47.5 million. This increase will be partially used to meet some debts, to equip the company and to activate our work," Salam added.
MEA is 99-percent owned by the central bank, Bank of Lebanon, under a $100 million debt-for-equity swap last September that wiped out the airline's debts accumulated between 1990 and 1995.
In the second tranche of the capital increase, the central bank contributed $31.25 million in November and will add a fourth tranche later to complete the $225 million increase.
Salam did not say when the remaining increase will be approved.
On Friday, he said he did not forsee a net profit being made by MEA before 1999.
"The company lost $50 million in 1996, and is expected to lose $20 million in 1997 before breaking even in 1998," he said.
